stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Draft
    Draft --> Resolving: first input submitted
    Draft --> Cancelled: discard draft
    Resolving --> Running: bindings validated and frozen snapshot committed
    Resolving --> BlockedDraft: unresolved requirement or validation failure
    BlockedDraft --> Resolving: bindings corrected and first input resubmitted
    BlockedDraft --> Cancelled: discard draft
    Running --> WaitingForInput: Wait for Input reached
    WaitingForInput --> Running: next ordered user input
    Running --> Paused: pause acknowledged at safe boundary
    Paused --> Running: resume same harness position
    Running --> AwaitingApproval: Approval node or configured action
    AwaitingApproval --> Running: approved
    AwaitingApproval --> Running: denied result routed by workflow
    Running --> Rehydrating: worker or application interruption
    WaitingForInput --> Rehydrating: application restart
    AwaitingApproval --> Rehydrating: application restart
    Paused --> Rehydrating: application restart
    Cancelling --> Rehydrating: interruption during cleanup
    Rehydrating --> Running: active checkpoint and committed cursor restored
    Rehydrating --> WaitingForInput: restored at wait
    Rehydrating --> AwaitingApproval: restored pending decision
    Rehydrating --> Paused: restored user pause
    Rehydrating --> Cancelling: restore committed cancel intent
    Running --> Cancelling: cancel requested
    Paused --> Cancelling: cancel requested
    AwaitingApproval --> Cancelling: cancel requested
    WaitingForInput --> Cancelling: cancel requested
    Cancelling --> Cancelled: process trees stopped and terminal event committed
    Running --> Completed: workflow completion
    Running --> Failed: terminal unhandled failure or exhausted limit
    Completed --> [*]
    Failed --> [*]
    Cancelled --> [*]
    note right of Running
      Retry current operation creates a new attempt in this Run.
      Editing or retrying older history forks a new Chat.
      Committed side effects are never replayed during recovery.
    end note
